problem_motivation.content: Degradation of structural materials in molten salt environments remains a critical concern for CSP systems, with high operating temperatures and reactive salts increasing corrosion susceptibility and reducing component lifetimes.

problem_motivation.content: The molten salt corrosion behavior of dual-phase HEAs and the fundamental understanding of underlying high-temperature corrosion mechanisms have not been reported.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, the molten salt corrosion behavior of dual phase HEAs for potential use in CSP systems has not been reported so far, and fundamental understanding of the underlying high-temperature corrosion mechanisms is lacking.

prior_approach.content: Previous studies have reported various EHEAs with excellent mechanical properties and some, like AlCoCrFeNi2.1, showed superior pitting corrosion resistance in chloride solutions at room temperature.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Some examples of EHEAs with excellent combination of strength and ductility include CoCrFeNiZr 0.5 , CoCrFeNiMnPd 1.4 , CoCrFeNiMnPd 0.6 , Nb 25 Sc 25 Ti 25 Zr 25 , AlCrFeNiMo 0.2 , Al 1.2 CrCuFeNi 2 and AlCoCrFeNi x [ [24] ]. In particular, the AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA with lamellar arrangement of BCC (B2) and FCC (L1 2 ) solid-solution phases has shown the most promising mechanical properties [ [22] , [25] , [26] , [27] ]. AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA showed superior pitting corrosion resistance compared to 304 stainless steel in chloride solution at room temperature [ [27] ]. This EHEA exhibited an excellent combination of high yield strength (~750 MPa) and ductility (elongation ~18%) at room temperature [ [22] , [28] ].

questions.question: Does the barrier mechanism of the FCC-L12 phase in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 hold when moisture is introduced to the molten salt environment, given that the current study lacks moisture data?
questions.rationale: The paper attributes protection to the FCC-L12 barrier but explicitly notes moisture effects were not evaluated; confirming this boundary is critical for applying the alloy in humid CSP conditions.
questions.decision_use: Determines if the alloy requires additional coating or moisture control strategies before deployment in real-world CSP systems.
answer_requirements: Measure corrosion rates of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 in molten salt with controlled moisture additions and compare to anhydrous conditions using weight gain.
evidence_spans: Additionally, the work function increased with increasing temperature for AlCoCrFeNi 2.1, indicating that the FCC-L1 2 phase acted as a barrier against further oxidation and protected the underlying BCC-B2 phase
However, a detailed evaluation of the effect of moisture content on corrosion behavior has not been performed in the current study

questions.decision_use: Guides whether to prioritize Al content optimization or microstructure control (phase fraction/interface engineering) for next-generation alloys.

questions.rationale: The alloy shows a massive advantage (9 vs 20 mm/year) now, but the lack of moisture data creates a risk of catastrophic failure in humid environments.
questions.decision_use: Sets the maximum allowable water partial pressure limit for component specifications or dictates the need for drying systems.

candidate.content: Aluminum acts as a sacrificial element, reducing the Cr dissolution rate by forming a redox couple (Al/AlCl3) that thermodynamically disfavors the dissolution of Co, Ni, and Fe.
candidate.evidence_span: This suggests that Al in the AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 acted as a sacrificial element and reduced Cr dissolution rate in the molten salt compared to DS2205. Redox control technique has been utilized for corrosion mitigation in molten fluoride and chloride salts. Dissolution of Al and Cr into the molten salt resulted in the formation of AlCl3 and CrCl2, which formed a redox couple of Al/AlCl3 and Cr/CrCl2. At the redox potential, Co, Ni, and Fe become relatively nobler and their dissolution is thermodynamically unfavorable.
